newsitem.title: USA: RESEARCH ALERT - Usiminas estimates cut.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT - Usiminas estimates cut.

text.p: -- Bear, Stearns & Co said it reduced its 1996 and 1997 earnings estimates for Brazilian steel company Usiminas' 144-A American Depositary Receipt (ADR), but maintained its attractive rating for the instrument.
-- The brokerage said it is reducing its 1996 earnings estimate for Usiminas to $1.01 per ADR from $1.57 and its 1997 estimate to $1.15 from $1.79.
-- The cuts are due to lower-than-expected first-half domestic market sales, lower export prices and higher fixed and operating costs, it said.

-- But it added second-half results for Usiminas and steel firm Cosipa, in which it holds a stake, should improve due to projections for higher volume sales, an average 4.5 percent price increase and a drops in fixed and operating costs.
-- "Looking at the future and from a structural point of view, Usiminas should post strong revenues due to a high proportion of sales in the domestic market and a better product mix," it said.
-- It added that operating costs should continue to shrink and, with Cosipa results improving, Usiminas also will benefit.
-- As a result, it said, the 144-A ADR is attractive with strong upside potential in the medium to longer-term.
-- Usiminas' preferred share was off 0.01 real at 1.03 reais and its voting common was flat at 0.98 real at noon/1100 EDT on the Sao Paulo stock exchange.
